Let $x_0$ be the real number such that $e^{x_0}+x_0=0$. For a given real number $\alpha$, define $g(x)=\frac{3 x e^x+3 x-\alpha e^x-\alpha x}{3\left(e^x+1\right)}$
for all real numbers $x$.
Then which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & e^{x_0}+x_0=0 \\ & g(x)=\frac{3 x e^x+3 x-\alpha e^x-\alpha x}{3\left(e^x+1\right)} \\ & g(x)=x-\frac{\alpha\left(e^x+x\right)}{3\left(e^x+1\right)}, g(x)+e^{x_0}=x+e^{x_0}-\frac{\alpha}{3}\left(\frac{e^x+x}{e^x+1}\right) \\ & g(x)+e^{x_0}=\left(x-x_0\right)-\frac{\alpha}{3}\left(\frac{e^x+x}{e^x+1}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \text{ As very clear } g\left(x_0\right)+x_0 \Rightarrow 0\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow x_0}\left|\frac{g(x)+e^{x_0}}{x-x_0}\right| \frac{0 \uparrow}{0 \uparrow}=\lim _{x \rightarrow x_0}\left|\frac{g^{\prime}(x)}{1}\right|=\left|g^{\prime}\left(x_0\right)\right| \\ & g^{\prime}(x)=1-\frac{\alpha}{3}\left(\frac{\left(e^x+1\right)\left(e^x+1\right)-\left(e^x+x\right) e^x}{\left(e^x+1\right)^2}\right) \\ & g^{\prime}\left(x_0\right)=1-\frac{\alpha}{3}\left(\frac{\left(e^{x_0}+1\right)^2}{\left(e^{x_0}+1\right)^2}\right)=1-\frac{\alpha}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow x_0}\left|\frac{g(x)+e^{x_0}}{x-x_0}\right|=\left|g^{\prime}\left(x_0\right)\right|=\left|^{1}-\frac{\alpha}{3}\right|\end{aligned}$

Let $S$ be the set of all $(\alpha, \beta) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ such that
$\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sin \left(x^2\right)\left(\log _e x\right)^\alpha \sin \left(\frac{1}{x^2}\right)}{x^{\alpha \beta}\left(\log _e(1+x)\right)^\beta}=0$.
Then which of the following is (are) correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sin x^2 \cdot\left(\log _e x\right)^\alpha \cdot \sin \frac{1}{x^2}}{x^{\alpha \beta} \cdot\left(\log _e(1+x)\right)^\beta}=0 \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left(\log _e x\right)^\alpha}{\left(\log _e(x+1)\right)^\beta \cdot x^{\alpha \beta+2}}=0\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{\log _e x}{\log _e(x+1)}\right)^\beta \cdot \frac{\left(\log _e x\right)^{\alpha-\beta}}{x^{\alpha \beta+2}}=0 \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left(\log _e x\right)^{\alpha-\beta}}{x^{\alpha \beta+2}}=0 \quad \text{ Put } \log _e x=t \\ & \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{t^{\alpha-\beta}}{\left(e^t\right)^{\alpha \beta+2}}=0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f: \left(0, 1\right) \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined as $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{n}$ if $x \in [ \dfrac{1}{n + 1}, \dfrac{1}{n} )$ where $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Let $g: \left(0, 1\right) \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that ${∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt < g\left(x\right) < 2\sqrt{x}$ for all $x \in \left(0, 1\right)$. Then $\lim_{x \to 0}f\left(x\right)g\left(x\right)$
questions.solution:
Given,

$f: \left(0, 1\right) \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined as $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{n}$ if $x \in [ \dfrac{1}{n + 1}, \dfrac{1}{n} )$ where $n \in \mathbb{N}$

And $g: \left(0, 1\right) \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that ${∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt < g\left(x\right) < 2\sqrt{x}$ for all $x \in \left(0, 1\right)$.

Now we need to solve $1$ sided limit here to get some answer, as $\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}$ doesn’t exist here (not in domain)

As $\dfrac{1}{n + 1} \le x < \dfrac{1}{n}$

$⇒ n + 1 \ge \dfrac{1}{x} > n$

$⇒ n \ge \dfrac{1}{x} - 1 ⇒ \sqrt{n} \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{x} - 1}$

So, let $f\left(x\right) = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - 1}$ where $\left(\cdot\right) =$ least integer function

Now multiplying $f\left(x\right)$ in ${∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt < g\left(x\right) < 2\sqrt{x}$ and taking limit we get,

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}{∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt \cdot \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - 1} \le \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f\left(x\right) \cdot g\left(x\right) \le \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - 1} \times 2\sqrt{x}$

Now $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - 1} \times 2\sqrt{x} = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}2\sqrt{x}\sqrt{\left[\dfrac{1}{x}\right]}\left(\dfrac{1}{x} \notin Z\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}2\sqrt{x\left(\dfrac{1}{x} - \left\{\dfrac{1}{x}\right\}\right)} = 2$

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}2\sqrt{1 - x\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)} = 2; \left(\dfrac{1}{x} \notin Z\right)$

So, $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}{∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt \cdot \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{x} - \left\{\dfrac{1}{x}\right\}} = \dfrac{{∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt \cdot \sqrt{1 - x\left\{\dfrac{1}{x}\right\}}}{\sqrt{x}}$

And $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{{∫}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - t}{t}}dt}{\sqrt{x}} = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - x}{x}} - 2x\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - {x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}}}{\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}}$

{Using L-hospital rule}

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}2\sqrt{1 - x} - 4\sqrt{x} \cdot \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}} = 2$

Similarly for $\dfrac{1}{x} \in Z$ is equal to $2$.

questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}g\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}\dfrac{2{\log}_{e}\left(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{\alpha}\right)}{{\log}_{e}\left({e}^{\sqrt{x}} - {e}^{\sqrt{\alpha}}\right)} = \lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}\dfrac{\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{\alpha}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right)}{\dfrac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{x}} - {e}^{\sqrt{\alpha}}}\left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}{e}^{\sqrt{x}}\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}\dfrac{{e}^{\sqrt{x}} - {e}^{\sqrt{\alpha}}}{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{\alpha}}\dfrac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{x}}} \cdot 2$

$= \dfrac{2}{{e}^{\sqrt{\alpha}}}\lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}\dfrac{{e}^{\sqrt{x}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}}{\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}} = 2$

$\lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}f\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = f\left(\lim_{x \to {\alpha}^{+}}g\left(x\right)\right)$

$= f\left(2\right) = sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0 . 50$
